answer: Bind each agent key to one physical CPU via confidential-compute attestation. Each epoch the agent's enclave (AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX) signs a fresh nonce with a chip-unique key chained to the vendor root. Twenty VMs on one ferrous rack server share a host chip, so they collapse into one seat. Each extra identity needs its own bare-metal box, about $60/month, so 100 clones cost $6,000 monthly. Failure mode: keys leaked by a firmware bug; quotes below the patched TCB level are refused on a 30-day horizon, and merged clusters show saffron on the explorer for jurors to audit.
